_comment: Curated, not exhaustive. Each entry is a real RPython helper with a precondition its signature doesn't enforce -- calling it with an out-of-precondition value produces PyPy's generic 'SystemError: unexpected internal exception (please report a bug)' leak instead of a proper app-level exception. Seeded from danzin's fusil findings (docs/PYPY_FINDINGS_REPORT.md); grow this list from future confirmed bugs, not speculation. See design doc §9.1. A helper whose precondition has independent clauses declares them in `clauses`: each is discharged separately, by a call-site keyword (`discharged_by_kwarg`), by a proactive text hint, or by a reactive `except` handler -- and a reactive guard counts only when EVERY name in `exception_guard_hints` is handled, since a partial handler is exactly the shape of confirmed bug #3. A call leaving ANY clause undischarged stays CONSIDER -- a range check must not clear a surrogate obligation. Helpers with no `clauses` key keep the original single-clause behaviour.

helpers.precondition: argument must be <= 0x10FFFF and, unless allow_surrogates=True is passed, not a surrogate (0xD800-0xDFFF)
helpers.confirmed_bug: struct.unpack('u', b'abcd') -- pypy/module/struct/formatiterator.py's append_utf8 passes r_uint(value) straight through with no range check at all. Second confirmed instance, surrogate clause only: format(0xD800, 'c') / f'{0xD800:c}' -- pypy/objspace/std/newformat.py:847 range-checks 0 <= value <= 0x10FFFF three lines above the call but omits allow_surrogates=True, so the 2048 surrogate codepoints pass the guard and leak SystemError. Reproduced on PyPy 7.3.23 (194f9f44b505); CPython 3.14.4 returns '\ud800'. Same shape reproduced in pypy/module/_csv/interp_csv.py via csv.reader(iter([]), delimiter='\ud800').

helpers.precondition: the 'signed' argument must actually match whether the bigint's value is negative -- passing signed=False (or leaving a stale/attacker-controlled state) for a negative value raises an internal OverflowError-shaped RPython exception, not the app-level OverflowError CPython raises
helpers.confirmed_bug: codecs.getincrementalencoder(<multibyte codec>)().setstate(-1) -- the state int is handed to rbigint.tobytes() with no sign check first

helpers.precondition: same as rbigint.tobytes -- module-level variant taking a plain int rather than an rbigint instance
helpers.confirmed_bug: same underlying shape as rbigint.tobytes; not itself the confirmed call site but sharing the same precondition

helpers.precondition: pos must be a valid byte offset into a well-formed UTF-8 string -- passing an offset that lands in the middle of a multi-byte sequence causes an internal RPython assertion instead of a proper app-level ValueError
codepoint must be in [0, 0x10FFFF] and not a surrogate unless allow_surrogates is explicitly set -- same shape as unichr_as_utf8
the slice indices must be valid byte offsets aligned to character boundaries in the target UTF-8 buffer; unaligned offsets cause internal RPython exceptions
byteorder must be 'big' or 'little' (not an arbitrary string); sign/unsigned mismatch when the high bit is set and signed=False causes internal OverflowError rather than ValueError
the value passed must fit in the target rarith type; overflow during narrowing conversion causes an internal RPython exception instead of an app-level OverflowError
the bigint value must fit in a machine int (sys.maxsize); if it does not, RPython raises an internal OverflowError instead of the app-level OverflowError CPython raises
the bigint value must be non-negative and fit in an unsigned machine int; negative values cause an internal RPython exception
the 'errors' argument must be one of the error handler strings PyPy's codec machinery supports; an unrecognised handler name causes an internal RPython lookup failure rather than a LookupError
input length must be non-negative and the error handler must be a recognised codec handler name

every byte in the input must be <= 127 unless a non-strict error handler is passed; bytes 128–255 cause an internal codec exception when errors='strict' is assumed at the call site without validating the input is clean ASCII
codepoints must all be in [0, 0x10FFFF]; surrogates require allow_surrogates=True or a surrogatepass error handler; the BOM flag must be consistent with the target encoding variant

the argument must already be a Python-level int that could overflow -- passing the result of an expression that cannot overflow is harmless but passing an expression that overflows before ovfcheck sees it means ovfcheck never fires; call sites that perform arithmetic in r_uint before calling ovfcheck silently truncate rather than overflow
the float must be in the range [INT_MIN, INT_MAX]; NaN and Inf both cause an internal RPython exception instead of the app-level OverflowError/ValueError CPython raises
the integer passed must be non-negative when the caller intends unsigned semantics; negative Python ints silently wrap to large unsigned values in RPython rather than raising

intmask silently truncates to the machine int range; callers that pass values expecting no truncation and then use the result in a range-sensitive context (array index, length) silently produce wrong values rather than raising
the unicode value must be a valid RPython unicode string with codepoints in [0, 0x10FFFF]; surrogates cause an internal RPython codec exception unless the caller explicitly allows them
build() must not be called after the builder has already been built or after a failed append; calling build() twice on the same builder is not safe in the translated build

the flags argument must be a valid combination of O_* constants for the host OS; invalid flag combinations map directly to the syscall and raise an internal RPython OSError instead of the app-level OSError with errno set
the signal number must be a valid signal for the host platform; signal numbers outside [1, NSIG) cause an internal RPython exception instead of the app-level OSError/ValueError CPython raises
both file descriptor arguments must be non-negative valid file descriptors; negative or out-of-range values cause internal RPython exceptions instead of app-level OSError
the input string must be a valid float literal; an invalid string causes an internal RPython ParseStringError rather than the app-level ValueError CPython raises

the format character must be one of 'e', 'E', 'f', 'F', 'g', 'G', 'r', 's', '%'; an unsupported format character causes an internal RPython ValueError instead of the app-level ValueError CPython raises
the float value must be finite (not NaN, not Inf); passing NaN or Inf causes an internal RPython exception in the dtoa C layer rather than a proper ValueError
the value must be a single-byte string or integer in [0, 255]; multi-byte or out-of-range values cause an internal RPython exception instead of the app-level struct.error CPython raises
the buffer must have at least one byte at the unpack offset; reading past the end of the buffer causes an internal RPython exception instead of a struct.error
the category argument must be one of the platform-valid LC_* constants; an invalid category value causes an internal RPython exception rather than the app-level locale.Error CPython raises
the byte string must be well-formed UTF-8; if allow_surrogates is not passed, surrogate codepoints in the input cause an internal CheckError instead of a UnicodeDecodeError with proper error position
the character argument must be a valid single-codepoint UTF-8 string; a multi-character or empty string causes an internal RPython assertion
only valid if the bigint fits in a C long; values outside [-2^63, 2^63-1] cause an internal RPython OverflowError rather than the app-level OverflowError CPython raises

the BOM or explicit byteorder argument must be consistent with the actual byte order of the input; a BOM mismatch or invalid byteorder string causes an internal RPython exception instead of a UnicodeDecodeError

same BOM/byteorder constraint as str_decode_utf_16; additionally, every 4-byte code unit must decode to a codepoint <= 0x10FFFF, since out-of-range values cause an internal exception rather than UnicodeDecodeError
